newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia cuts oil deliveries to Bulgarian refinery.
newsitem.headline: Russia cuts oil deliveries to Bulgarian refinery.

text.p: Russia's Rosneft said on Tuesday that it had cut crude oil supplies to Bulgaria's largest oil refinery, Neftohim, over unpaid debts and political uncertainty.

Valentin Zlatev, head of Rosneft's export department, said that only one 70,000-tonne vessel of oil had gone to Neftohim in January out of a planned four, and that future deliveries were in question until debts were repaid.
"We're negotiating a (debt repayment) programme and after that, we will fix supplies for February," he said.

He said agreements had not yet been reached partly because of political unrest in the Balkan state, where the government has been paralysed since December when Socialist Prime Minister Zhan Videnov resigned.
Rosneft, the Russian state-owned oil company that is being privatised, supplies oil directly to the refinery through its Rosbulneft joint venture with Neftohim.
Neftohim's annual refining capacity is about 7.5 million tonnes and it supplies about 70 percent of the domestic market, according to company officials.
